item.title: Report – Juventus Identify Three January Transfer Priorities
item.description: Report – Juventus Identify Three January Transfer Priorities Juventus are preparing for a busy January transfer window, with Luciano Spalletti keen to strengthen three key positions as he looks to improve the squad for the second half of the season. According to La Gazzetta dello Sport , the Bianconeri have identified a center-forward, a central midfielder and a left-back as their main priorities. The club must also consider potential departures, as every new arrival could depend on an outgoing transfer. Spalletti’s biggest demand remains a traditional number nine. Alexander Sorloth has emerged as Juventus’ preferred option, with the Atletico Madrid striker still high on their shortlist after attracting interest last summer. Folarin Balogun and Mateo Retegui are also on the club’s shortlist, but Juventus are unlikely to convince their clubs to let them leave midway through the season. Our take on Juventus & January transfer window The Italian coach also wants another midfielder following a difficult start to the campaign. Manuel Locatelli and Khephren Thuram are both expected to return in 2027, leaving Juventus short of options in the meantime. Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg, Darryl Bakola, and Issa Doumbia are among the names under consideration, although a move for the latter could prove particularly complicated. The final priority concerns the left side of defense. Rayan Ait-Nouri, Destiny Udogie , and Alejandro Balde feature on Juventus’ shortlist, with the Barcelona defender considered an ambitious target. Juan Cabal’s recent improvement could influence the club’s plans, while Andrea Cambiaso’s future may also become relevant.

item.title: Newark Charter earns top seed in Class 1A football playoffs
item.description: Playing its second season of varsity football, Newark Charter finished the regular season undefeated and earned the top seed in the DIAA Class 1A Football Tournament. The 10-0 Patriots will host eighth-seeded Concord when the playoffs begin Friday, Nov. 20 at 7 p.m. The Patriots reached the Class 1A championship a season ago and lost to Seaford in overtime 21-20 . The DIAA announced its three football tournament brackets Sunday, Nov. 15, the day after the conclusion of the regular season. More information on the Class 3A and Class 2A brackets can be found at delawareonline.com. Joining Newark Charter and Concord in the Class 1A playoffs are Brandywine, Conrad, Seaford, Newark, Charter of Wilmington and Dickinson. Here is what you need to know. https://public.flourish.studio/visualisation/30925038/visualisation.json?ref=embed-script When do Delaware's Class 1A football playoffs begin? The Class 3A playoffs begin Friday, Nov. 20. Games will be hosted by the higher seeds. Here is the complete first round schedule: No. 8 Concord (6-4) at No. 1 Newark Charter (10-0), Nov. 20 7 p.m. No. 7 Dickinson (6-4) at No. 2 Brandywine (6-4), Nov. 20 7 p.m. No. 6 Charter of Wilmington (6-4) at No. 3 Conrad (6-4), Nov. 21 11 a.m. No. 5 Newark (6-4) at No. 4 Seaford (8-2), Nov. 21 7 p.m. The playoffs will continue the following weekend with semifinals on Friday, Nov. 27 and Saturday, Nov. 28 at higher seeds. When is the Class 1A football championship? The Class 1A football championship is scheduled for Saturday, Dec. 5 at Delaware State's Alumni Stadium at 11 a.m. The Class 2A title game will follow at 5 p.m. The Class 3A championship is scheduled for Friday, Dec. 4 at 7 p.m. at Alumni Stadium. Who won the Class 1A championship in 2025? Seaford defeated Newark Charter in overtime 21-20. It was Seaford's first football state championship since 1983. Who are the top contenders in Class 1A? Newark Charter and Seaford are once again the top contenders. They were ranked first and second in Class 1A throughout the regular season. Newark Charter beat Seaford in Newark 20-0 on Oct. 23. https://public.flourish.studio/visualisation/30899049/visualisation.json?ref=embed-script How do I buy tickets to DIAA football playoff games? Tickets for the DIAA football state tournaments will be available for purchase online via GoFan, the official ticket platform of the DIAA . Children 4 years old and younger are admitted without charge to all games. The DIAA said ticket links will be posted by Tuesday, Nov. 17 at 8 a.m. Championship games will be streamed live on the NFHS Network . Brandon Holveck reports on high school sports for The News Journal. Contact him at bholveck@delawareonline.com . item.description: MUNICH, Germany — The first big cheer for Detroit Lions receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown at Allianz Arena came before kickoff when he ran out of the tunnel carrying a German flag. The next and loudest was on Detroit's opening drive, when he left Christian Gonzalez in the dust with a vicious juke and cut upfield, racing all the way to the end zone with defenders trying to bring him down from behind for a 56-yard touchdown — the first of two scores on the day for St. Brown — as almost the entire stadium rose to their feet and let out a roar for their favorite (American) footballing grandson . In any other game, in any other place, maybe St. Brown would have been caught on the third-longest touchdown of his career. But after bursting into open field, it was obvious that nobody would deny St. Brown the end zone in Munich, and even following an injury to defensive end Aidan Hutchinson , nobody was going to deny the Lions in a 35-10 victory, Detroit's fifth straight win, moving the Lions (7-2) into first place in the NFC North. St. Brown scored a second touchdown with 8:16 left in the third quarter to put Detroit up 28-3, and a Patriots fan in front of the press box wearing a Drake Maye jersey raised his arms to celebrate. Amid talks of whether this would be a pro-Lions or pro-Patriots crowd (it was heavily slanted toward the latter), only a small fraction of the Munich-record 70,225 fans in attendance were not pro-St. Brown. His German-born mother, Miriam, was the belle of the ball in Munich this week, a long way from her hometown of Leverkusen but feeling right at home as what felt like the entire country showered her son with adoration. He finished with four catches for 98 yards and two touchdowns. "It's great," Miriam told The Detroit News earlier this week. "This is not my hometown, but it's still great. It's wonderful." item.title: AFC playoff standings: Browns move up early in Week 10, down now only option this week
item.description: The Cleveland Browns Week 10 game versus the Houston Texans has huge implications for the AFC playoff picture . Heading into this week, the Browns were tied with the New England Patriots for the final playoff seed in the conference , losing out on the spot due to a tiebreaker, despite losing two straight games. While we await kickoff in Cleveland’s game versus Houston, the Patriots were playing the Detroit Lions over in Germany. Early in the game, both teams lost key players when DE Aidan Hutchinson injured QB Drake Maye during a sack, then injured himself while celebrating that sack. While the Hutchinson injury is a big deal long term, New England’s loss of Maye to an ankle injury all but finished off any hopes they had of securing a victory this week. The Lions ended up controlling the rest of the game, leading to the lopsided 35-10 final score. With the loss, the Patriots drop to 5-5 and are a half game behind the Browns, who move up to the seventh seed. No matter what happens the rest of Week 10, Cleveland cannot move up any higher in the AFC playoff standings, with the rest of the conference’s elites having two or fewer losses on the season. If the Browns beat the Texans, moving to 6-4, they will be a game up on New England. If Cleveland loses, the Las Vegas Raiders and Baltimore Ravens have a chance to move into a four-way tie for the seventh seed, along with the Browns and Patriots. If that happens, we will have the official tiebreaker information after the Ravens game on Monday Night Football. A Houston victory will help them climb just a game behind the final playoff spot. A lot of “if” outcomes in Week 10. For now, the Cleveland Browns technically have the seventh seed in the AFC, with a chance to solidify that spot with a victory over the Houston Texans in Week 10.

item.description: Ashley Tumlin-Imagn Images Dabo Swinney’s disappointing Clemson season gets even worse with catastrophic Tait Reynolds injury update appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . It has been a disaster of a season for Clemson and Dabo Swinney . Clemson has deal wth a ton of injuries all year long , and on Saturday, they fell to Georgia Tech. Tait Reynolds got the start at quarterback for Clemson, but lasted just one drive before being injured. Now, an update is being given on the quarterback , per On3. “Clemson starting QB Tait Reynolds has suffered a ligament tear in his left knee and will undergo surgery,” the update read. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Reynolds attempted just one pass against Georgia Tech, good for a three-yard completion. He also ran once for 24 yards. He took over as the starting quarterback for Clemson on September 19 against North Carolina. Reynolds has completed 156 of 241 passes for 1,449 yards and three touchdowns. He also has four interceptions. Reynolds, a freshman, was replaced by senior Trent Pearman. He completed just two of six passes for six yards before he was removed from the game. That led to Christopher Vizzina jumping in at quarterback. He completed 12 of 27 passes for 133 yards with an interception. Vizzina suffered a concussion and went to the hospital after the game. He was already dealing with a left ankle injury and was dressed as an emergency quarterback for the game. Now, Clemson needs to figure out who will be at quarterback on Friday night against Duke. Swinney could go back to Pearman, or send out freshman Brock Bradley. The team also has Chris Denson, who moved from quarterback to wide receiver in the offseason. Regardless, it will be a difficult test against a Duke defense allowing just 15.3 points per game. item.title: Barcelona closely monitoring the progress of Serie A rising star – report
item.description: Barcelona closely monitoring the progress of Serie A rising star – report It is no secret that Barcelona are in the market for a new centre-back ahead of the January transfer window. The injuries to Eric Garcia, Jules Kounde, and Andreas Christensen have highlighted the club’s lack of depth at centre-back. The club, therefore, are now keen on finding a new centre-back, having most recently been linked with a move for Bayern Munich star Jonathan Tah. Barcelona keeping an eye on Juan Rodriguez According to Diario SPORT , Barcelona are closely monitoring the progress of Serie A’s rising star, Juan Rodriguez. Juan Rodriguez has emerged as a rising star in Serie A. (Photo by Marco Rosi – SS Lazio/Getty Images) A centre-back by trade, Rodriguez has impressed onlookers with his ball-playing ability and versatility, as he can also operate as a left-back. With 13 appearances this season in all competitions, the 21-year-old is already a first-team regular at Cagliari and fits the profile Barcelona are looking for: young, left-footed, and versatile. The report suggests Rodriguez is seen as the future of the Uruguayan national team, a country that has produced multiple defensive leaders in the past, including La Liga and Atletico Madrid legend Diego Godin. Can Barça sign Rodriguez? Juan Rodriguez has impressed onlookers with his versatility. (Photo by Paolo Bruno/Getty Images) Acquiring the services of Juan Rodriguez from Cagliari, though, won’t be as straightforward. The defender has a long-term contract at the Italian club, running until 2030, meaning they would have to negotiate directly with Cagliari. But having only signed the player last year, it is unlikely that the Italian club will want to part ways with the defender so soon, and even if they do, they are likely to ask for a fortune. Signing Rodriguez will be even more tricky in the upcoming January transfer window, as Cagliari have yet to show any desire to cash in on the Uruguayan so far. Then, there is the question of value. Cagliari signed Rodriguez for just €5 million, while the defender’s current value, as per Transfermarkt, stands at €14 million. The club are likely to ask for a significantly higher amount, given his age profile and potential.

Russell missed the conversion, but he missed something - or somebody - else just after and it proved costly. One of the many things holding Scotland back is how easy they are to score against - and here was another case for the prosecution. Rob Valetini and Gordon helped put the Wallabies on the front foot but, when they swept to the left touchline, the whole thing might have come to a halt had Russell made his tackle on Potter. They butchered a big opportunity from a close-range lineout - losing their own throw - then won it back and got turned over at the breakdown. Australia scored in the last seconds when Jorgensen ran in after a beautiful offload from Jeremy Williams. Ben Donaldson put over the conversion to make it 15-12. The ‘Cats held the Buckeyes below both of these standards and became just the third team all season to hold Ryan Day’s offense to under 400 yards. It was on the offensive end where the ’Cats had their major struggles. For the second week in a row, NU set its lowest single-game offensive yardage total of the season, finishing the contest with just 278 yards. The ‘Cats’ biggest offensive problems came on the ground. NU finished Saturday’s tilt with 53 yards on 29 carries (which includes Marchiol’s 10 scrambles for -15 yards), its second-worst rushing performance of the season and its first time finishing with under 100 yards on the ground since its Week 4 loss to Indiana. Like the rest of the team, Northwestern’s signal-caller had no lack of belief in himself. item.title: 'That's a false stat': Shai Gilgeous-Alexander corrects reporter's AI mistake
item.description: Credit: Oklahoma City Thunder Oklahoma City Thunder All-Star guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is the reigning back-to-back NBA MVP. Gilgeous-Alexander is also now the NBA’s preeminent Anti-AI King. On Friday, the Thunder suffered a 113-112 loss to the Los Angeles Clippers despite Gilgeous-Alexander dropping 40 points. It was a night to forget for Oklahoma City, until the final question of Gilgeous-Alexander’s postgame press conference created a clip that will live forever. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander fact-checking an LA reporter who used AI search results to get an incorrect stat lmao https://t.co/B4wZbSFv7B — Clemente Almanza (@CAlmanza1007) November 14, 2026 “Shai, during the first half, it was the first time in your NBA career that you didn’t record a single assist,” an off-camera reporter said. “At what point during the game — I mean, you ended the game with 40 — do you feel like you have to turn that up a notch and start taking over the game offensively?” “Wait, one more time? It was— wait, what?” Gilgeous-Alexander inquired, peering over his glasses quizzically. The reporter repeated that Gilgeous-Alexander’s failure to record an assist in the first half against the Clippers marked the first such instance of his decorated career. “That’s a false stat, by the way,” Gilgeous-Alexander said. “In Game 4 against Indiana, I didn’t have an assist the whole game. But sorry. Go ahead.” It’s true. In Game 4 of the 2025 NBA Finals against the Indiana Pacers, Gilgeous-Alexander posted 35 points, three rebounds, three steals, and one block, but zero assists. The reporter repeated his actual question, which Gilgeous-Alexander answered. “Gotcha,” the reporter said once Gilgeous-Alexander finished. “Don’t trust AI.” Gilgeous-Alexander smiled and laughed, saying, “Yeah, don’t do it. Definitely don’t do it!” Clemente Almanza, lead writer for OKC Thunder Wire, was at the presser and described the reporter only as “ an LA reporter .” As of this writing, he has not been identified beyond that, which is probably for the best. While the predominant lesson here is to never rely on AI for research — or any journalistic function — it also calls back to evergreen advice from the great Kevin Van Valkenburg, formerly of ESPN and now at Fried Egg Golf . “A great journalism lesson: If you are trying to get good answers from someone in an interview, one of the worst ways to do it is long-ass questions designed to make you (the interviewer) feel or look smart,” Van Valkenburg wrote in May. Mandatory Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images The Kansas City Chiefs had a scary moment last weekend when star quarterback Patrick Mahomes took a big hit to his throwing arm during a 35-12 win over the New York Jets. Mahomes stayed in the game, and an MRI reportedly didn’t reveal any major damage, but the Chiefs weren’t taking any chances with his elbow. According to a new report, the team went outside of football for help this week, having two renowned baseball doctors review the scans of Mahomes’ elbow. The doctors reportedly found a muscle strain and a minor UCL sprain, and one of them felt that the Chiefs and Mahomes “got away with one.” Mahomes’ Injury Scare Late in the second quarter of last Sunday’s game, Jets edge rusher David Bailey hit Mahomes’ right arm as he was throwing, sacking him for the second time in three plays. Mahomes was down on the field for a moment before walking off slowly with his arm hanging at his side. But the two-time MVP flexed his elbow on the sideline, threw a few warm-up passes, and got back into the game. He finished 23 of 31 for 242 yards and two touchdowns, and the Chiefs improved to 6-2 on the season. After the game, Mahomes admitted that the injury scared him , especially after the knee injury that ended his season last year. But he also said he could tell pretty quickly that it wasn’t anything too serious. “Any time it’s elbows and knees, it’s always scary, just because you just don’t know,” Mahomes said, via ESPN’s Nate Taylor . “Even my knee last year, after we were doing the initial test, I thought, because I could walk off the field, I was going to be good. Then, all of a sudden, you do one test, and you’re just out [for the rest of the season]. That stuff scares you. Once I could throw the ball, I knew it wasn’t a ligament and it was more muscles.” ‘Got Away With One’ While Mahomes might not have thought the injury was all that serious, the Chiefs weren’t going to take any chances. According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter , the Chiefs had their own doctors review the scans, but they also had doctors from the Kansas City Royals and Texas Rangers offer second and third opinions. The doctors found that Mahomes suffered a muscle strain and what one source described as “a very small sprain of his UCL.” All of them believed it was safe for Mahomes to keep playing, even though he was sore and received treatment throughout the week. The two doctors were Dr. Vincent Key, the Royals’ head team physician who specializes in Tommy John surgery and newer UCL repair techniques, and Dr. Keith Meister, the Rangers’ team physician and one of baseball’s best-known orthopedic surgeons. According to Schefter, the Chiefs turned to baseball because the team felt that baseball deals with elbow injuries more than football does. Rick Burk

item.title: AFC Wimbledon, a failed £87m investment bid and the challenge for fan ownership
item.description: Clubs with wealthy proprietors can maintain a loss-making operation but things can be more complex when the supporters carry the can When you walk up from Haydons Road train station to Plough Lane there is a blue AFC Wimbledon billboard that reads “Fan owned football”, directly opposite the site of the old Plough Lane stadium where there are now blocks of flats. There is a memorial to the old Wimbledon FC – a reminder that supporters can often have little say in the running of their club – on the same corner, just up the road from the new Cherry Red Records Stadium. AFC Wimbledon are one of only two majority fan-owned clubs in the EFL – along with Exeter City – but that makes running a loss-making operation, as 94% of teams in England’s top five tiers are doing according to the State of the Game report, even more challenging. “In other clubs, the owner just puts their hand in their pocket, produces cash,” said Hannah Kitcher, who has been a member of the Dons Trust Board (DTB), which runs AFC Wimbledon, for seven years. “It’s harder when the owners are fans – you can only go to them so many times.” Continue reading...

item.title: De la Fuente feels the strain as Lamine Yamal club v country debate rages in Spain
item.description: Head coach hits out at ‘lies’ as suggestions of preferential treatment for young star overshadow preparations for England game in Madrid From the London Palladium to Madrid’s Metropolitano, they’re all here. On Sunday night, the footballers who lifted the game’s biggest awards meet again three weeks later and on the field this time, dinner jackets but not a single man left behind. Harry Kane, the Ballon d’Or and Gerd Müller trophy winner. Unai Simón, holder of the Lev Yashin award . Luis de la Fuente , the coach of the year who on Thursday night announced that also joining them will be Lamine Yamal , the kid who lifted the Kopa award as the best young player for the third year running and said he would have preferred Pau Cubarsí to be standing there instead. And, yes, Cubarsí will be there too for the final Nations League group game. At 1.45pm on Friday the world and European champions landed back at Madrid’s Barajas airport from Prague, where they had won again, before making their way by bus to their Las Rozas HQ, around the M40 motorway to the north-west of the capital. At about the same time, Lamine Yamal arrived from Barcelona, due in at midday. As was Mikel Oyarzabal , scorer of the winner at Euro 2024 and Spain’s top marksman this summer (not that he would ever tell you so) from San Sebastián. At 7.30pm, they trained, preparing to meet the World Cup semi-finalists and the team they defeated in Berlin at the end of Euro 2024. Two starters from the World Cup final will be absent: Dani Olmo and the captain, 2024 Ballon d’Or winner Rodri , are injured. But everyone else will be there. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Taking a brief minute to remember Pierre Sage’s impact at Crystal Palace
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! So farewell then, Pierre Sage . Many coaches leave under a cloud, not many have their departures completely obscured by the foul, retch-inducing one emanating from another team’s managerial circus, but such was Sage’s fate . The news section of Crystal Palace’s website helpfully tells you the amount of time it might take you to read each story it links through to. For example it should take four minutes or so to get through Tuesday’s “On this day: five big Crystal Palace birthdays”. “England: I love a knee slide!” will take you five. “Prize draw: be a mascot for our next [Bigger Vase] tie!” is a two-minute job. The statement informing the world of Sage’s exit? One minute. Eighty-three words. By way of illustration, the word “words” was the 84th of this paragraph. Just because the man’s French doesn’t mean his exit should be marked with a shrug. As I have been away at a conference, giving a presentation that the MC described as ‘sobering’, I’ve missed the last few days of football, so I was very sad to read about the passing of the great Danny Kelly . Others are far better placed to give tributes to the great man, but for younger generations who can’t comprehend the football cultural significance, Baker and Kelly represented the peak of football phone-ins. Before it became people ranting and raving about wanting the manager sacked as they’ve lost a few games or wanting the club to spend another few hundred million pounds on yet more players, it was about football supporters and supporting, from fans who actually went to games. Their peak was on BBC Radio in the 1990s, and there are too many examples of their greatness, but if I had to pick one, just one to illustrate it, it would, of course, be Gordon the Dundee United supporter and his bow tie . Rest in Peace, Danny Kelly. You gave us such joy” – Noble Francis. As they no longer seem to be ‘Dr Tottenham’, I was wondering if they had maybe passed the soubriquet on. I think the England cricket team has provided the answer (again)” – Andrew Parker. Impressive list of kiss-off press releases ( yesterday’s Football Daily ) but why was Ralf Rangnick omitted from the chronological list of post-Fergie managers? Is it because Football Daily valued him as little as Manchester United fans did?” – Mike Wilner. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. Before it became people ranting and raving about wanting the manager sacked as they’ve lost a few games or wanting the club to spend another few hundred million pounds on yet more players, it was about football supporters and supporting, from fans who actually went to games. Their peak was on BBC Radio in the 1990s, and there are too many examples of their greatness, but if I had to pick one, just one to illustrate it, it would, of course, be Gordon the Dundee United supporter and his bow tie . item.title: Manchester City’s weaknesses under Enzo Maresca are being exposed
item.description: After three straight defeats, City’s manager says he will use the international break to reassess. Their problems may go beyond tactics Sign up for our free newsletter here Enzo Maresca seemed, if not quite baffled by his side’s Saturday defeat to Nottingham Forest, then at least a little put out. After seven straight wins from the start of the season, that’s now three straight defeats, a pattern so unusual that it’s been recorded only once before in top-flight English history, by Sheffield Wednesday in 1904-05. The three defeats were all different, Maresca said, although in all of them City had had more possession and more chances. In the 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa two weeks ago, City had 63% of the ball and had 15 chances to Villa’s eight. In the 1-0 home defeat to Brighton last weekend, they had 62% possession and 21 chances to seven. At the City Ground, it was 79% possession and 12 chances to 11. So Maresca is right in one way: City could look at basic statistics and say they had been unfortunate – although Forest could equally point to the fact that they went into that game third top of the expected goals table but second-bottom of the actual table. item.title: That’s a Mora: Rodrigo and Roma rise with Lazio to give Eternal City new life | Nicky Bandini
item.description: Roma and Lazio have both made unbeaten starts to the Serie A season, giving those in the Italian capital dreams of a Scudetto After nine games in 28 days, Gian Piero Gasperini finally got a moment to pause and reflect on Sunday night. The Roma manager was back in Liguria, where he worked for the best part of a decade across two stints at Genoa, to collect an award from Stelle Nello Sport – an association formed to promote sport in the region – celebrating his career achievements and commitment to courageous attacking football. The timing worked out well. Gasperini’s Roma thumped Sassuolo 3-0 on Saturday, bouncing back from a midweek defeat against Manchester United . That result meant the Giallorossi had scored 31 times in 11 Serie A games. In the past 65 years only two Italian teams – the Juventus and Napoli sides of 2017-18 – had made a more prolific start to a top-flight campaign. More importantly, Roma’s victory meant they remained undefeated in domestic competition this season. Just like their neighbours Lazio, who drew 1-1 away against Napoli in the early kick-off on Sunday. Continue reading...

item.title: Football comes together across Spain to honour Jesús de Miguel: ‘We’ve seen how fragile life is’
item.description: Across La Liga and beyond this weekend, footballers took to the field knowing it could have been them In the final few minutes before stepping into the arena once more, heading out for his 199th Osasuna match on Saturday evening, the man who has scored more first division goals than anyone in their history stopped his teammates for a moment and told them what it meant to wear the shirt. “This is very important,” Ante Budimir began as the dressing room, their sanctuary, fell silent around him. “We don’t have this shirt today for the sake of it. He was not chosen, and nor are we. It could have happened to anyone, anyone. Let us go knowing that we’re grateful to be on the pitch: playing, watching, warming up, sitting on the bench, whatever it may be. Boys, we were not chosen: not us, not him. Let us go, gratefully. Without thought. We have a grand day before us.” With that, Osasuna’s players turned left out of the room, where they were joined in the tunnel by footballers from Athletic Club, rivals from the north, and together they went out past the little shrine of Saint Fermin on to the field. They carried white lilies and all wore the same white shirts with a No 9 on the back, a black ribbon and the name of Jesús de Miguel, the Tenerife striker who died after a collision on the pitch five days earlier at the age of 30. item.title: Rise of the ‘schooligans’: how a wave of antisocial behaviour threatens non-league football
item.description: Teenage ultras are increasingly causing disorder and communities fear it will not be long before it becomes something more dangerous It is five past three on Saturday afternoon and the teenage ultras of Hednesford Town are running late. They have arrived in Chester for their team’s National League North fixture and have hailed taxis, determined to make their presence felt at the ground. But word appears to have got out about their arrival. As one car turns away from the city’s charming half-timbered houses and into narrow residential streets, half a dozen local youths appear, haring round the corner in balaclavas. They try to attack the cab and chase after it as it pulls away. The smell of pyro is everywhere. As the taxi finally gets clear, the Chester gang stops in the middle of the road, shouting and gesticulating. One lad, no older than 16, pulls a long blade from inside his trousers and brandishes it. The incident ended there and no one was hurt, though a police investigation has been launched. The match went off without trouble too and the Hednesford gang – known at home as the “schooligans” – were escorted safely back to the station by Cheshire police. It was just another weekend in English non-league football, where a wave of antisocial behaviour is causing concern and leading the UK Football Policing Unit (UKFPU) to declare it its “most important” priority. As the disorder continues, a question remains: how long will it be before teenage trouble-making becomes something more dangerous? Continue reading...

item.title: Billions in revenue proves Fifa right on the World Cup – but only on things it cares about
item.description: The 2026 edition of the tournament brought in untold amounts of money to Gianni Infantino’s governing body The total hasn’t entirely stopped rising yet, still clicking away towards a final tally. Still, Fifa has already announced that it surpassed its own lofty revenue projections for the 2026 World Cup, bringing in $15bn, significantly more than anticipated. It appears that a third of that total – $5bn – came from ticket sales and hospitality alone, per reporting from the Times . That would mean direct income from the matchgoing fans came in five times as high in the United States, Canada and Mexico as it did at the last World Cup, in Qatar in 2022, when the total stood at $929m. While 2026’s expanded World Cup added 40 games to the schedule, the takings nevertheless went from an average of about $14.5m per match to about $48m. Continue reading...

item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
